We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> break amide to give acid and aniline (aniline attached to phenyl). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: amide bond between carbonyl (from unsaturated acid) and aniline (aniline). So precursor 1: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid: /C=C/C(=O) (attached to phenyl). Actually the unsaturated acid is (E)-3-(phenylamino)acrylic acid? Wait structure: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . So the acid part is (E)-3-(phenylamino)acrylic acid? Actually the carbonyl attached to N of aniline. So the acid is (E)-cinnamic acid derivative? The forward amide formation: carboxylic acid + aniline -> amide. So retrosynthetic precursor: the acid is (E)-3-(phenylamino)acrylic acid? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). So the acid would be (E)-cinnamic acid (C6H5-CH=CH-COOH) but with an aniline attached to carbonyl? Actually the amide is C(=O)N-aryl. So the acid is (E)-cinnamic acid (C6H5-CH=CH-COOH). Then coupling with aniline (c3ccccc3N) gives amide. Yes that matches: the product has /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH? Wait the SMILES: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N . So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl with an NH (aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl that also has an NH (i.e., an aniline with an extra NH2). Actually c3ccccc3N indicates an aniline (para? not specified). So the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline ring that also has an NH2 substituent (maybe ortho). So the amide formation uses aniline (with NH2) as nucleophile, reacting with the acid to give amide, leaving the NH2 on the ring unchanged.

Thus step 1: amide formation between cinnamic acid (or (E)-cinnamic acid) and 2-aminophenyl (aniline). So precursor: (E)-cinnamic acid (C6H5-CH=CH-COOH) and 2-aminobenzene (or aniline). But the aniline is part of the product; we keep it as same.

Step 2: Doebner modification to make the cinnamic acid from aromatic aldehyde (benzaldehyde) and malonic acid. So precursor: benzaldehyde (or substituted) and malonic acid. The aromatic aldehyde is likely p-tolyl? Actually the aromatic ring attached to the unsaturated chain is phenyl (c3ccccc3). No substituents. So aldehyde is benzaldehyde.

Thus step 2: benzaldehyde + malonic acid -> (E)-cinnamic acid.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: attach sulfonyl chloride to aniline on other phenyl ring. The target has sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings: NS(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). The sulfonyl chloride would be p-toluenesulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl group attached to phenyl ring with methyl (C) at para? The SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1 . So first phenyl ring has a methyl (para?) and sulfonamide linking to second phenyl ring (which is attached to unsaturated chain). So sulfonyl chloride precursor: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl). Reaction with aniline (the aniline on second phenyl? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to first phenyl ring (the one with methyl) and to sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So the sulfonyl chloride is attached to second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So we need sulfonyl chloride: 4-(... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride? The second phenyl has the unsaturated chain attached at para? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 . So the sulfonyl chloride would be 4-(cinnamoyl)phenylsulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to that phenyl ring at position where the sulfonamide nitrogen attaches. So the sulfonyl chloride is 4-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride (p-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride). So step 3: sulfonyl chloride (p-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride) reacts with aniline (the first phenyl ring with methyl) to give sulfonamide.

Thus retrosynthetic disconnections:

Target -> break sulfonamide: gives sulfonyl chloride (p-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride) + p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline). Actually the aniline is the first phenyl with methyl (Cc1ccc(N)cc1). So precursor 3: p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride (p-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride).

Then sulfonyl chloride can be derived from the corresponding sulfonic acid (p-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonic acid) via conversion to chloride (e.g., SOCl2). But we can consider sulfonyl chloride as available.

Now the sulfonyl chloride contains the cinnamic acid moiety attached to phenyl via sulfonyl group. That cinnamic acid part is from step 2 (cinnamic acid). So we need to generate the sulfonyl chloride from p-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonic acid, which can be made from p-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride? Might be okay to assume sulfonyl chloride is a commercial building block derived from the cinnamic acid via sulfonation? But we can propose that the sulfonyl chloride is made from the corresponding sulfonic acid which is made from sulfonation of the phenyl ring (electrophilic aromatic substitution) using SO3. However that's beyond 3 steps.

Given requirement of exactly 3 reactions, we can define:

Step A (retro): amide bond cleavage -> cinnamic acid + 2-aminophenyl (aniline). (Reaction type: amide formation forward)

Step B (retro): cinnamic acid from benzaldehyde + malonic acid via Doebner modification (forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). So retro: break C=C and COOH to give benzaldehyde and malonic acid.

Step C (retro): sulfonamide bond cleavage -> p-toluidine + p-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride. (forward: sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide)

Thus we need templates for these three transformations. We need to retrieve template IDs for each.

Search for amide formation template (carboxylic acid + amine). Use functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, functional_groups_formed: amide. Already tried but got empty. Maybe need to specify functional_groups_broken: ['aliphatic carboxylic acid'] and formed: ['amide'] but result empty. Could be that template exists but not returned due to limited dataset. Could try search without specifying formed.
